mcqs.question: A message keeps failing to process. What's the standard safe pattern for handling it?
options: Retry with backoff up to a bounded limit, then move the message to a dead-letter queue for manual or automated triage
Retry indefinitely until the message eventually succeeds
Immediately discard any message that fails on its first processing attempt
Pause the entire queue until an engineer manually intervenes
mcqs.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating exhausted messages to a DLQ handles both transient failures (a few retries clear them) and permanent ones (they get contained instead of blocking everything). Infinite retry is the failure mode itself, discarding on the first failure loses recoverable messages, and pausing the whole queue is far more disruptive than isolating just the one bad message.

mcqs.question: A malformed JSON payload fails deserialization every single time on a FIFO/ordered queue. What happens without a retry limit, and what changes with one?
options: The queue automatically detects malformed JSON and skips it without any configuration needed
Without a limit, it retries forever and blocks every message behind it; with a retry cap and a DLQ, it's isolated within seconds and the queue keeps moving
The malformed message is silently dropped by the broker after exactly one failed attempt
The consumer crashes permanently and needs to be manually restarted regardless of retry configuration
mcqs.explanation: Without a bound, the ordered queue stalls entirely behind the unprocessable message; a retry cap plus DLQ contains the damage to that one message within seconds. Brokers don't auto-detect or auto-drop malformed payloads on their own, and a well-configured consumer with retry limits doesn't need a manual restart to recover.

mcqs.question: Can DLQ triage be automated instead of a human reviewing every message?
options: All DLQ triage should always be fully automated with no human review
Automation should never be used for DLQ triage, since every failure needs human judgment
Known failure signatures can be auto-republished, but a novel failure reason should still page a human the first time it's seen
DLQ messages should automatically be redelivered to the original queue after a fixed delay regardless of cause
mcqs.explanation: Automating the recognized, well-understood failure patterns frees people to focus on genuinely new ones, which still need judgment the first time they appear. Full automation risks silently mishandling an unrecognized failure, refusing all automation wastes effort on well-understood cases, and blind redelivery after a fixed delay ignores whether the failure was even transient.

mcqs.question: A team retries a failing message indefinitely, reasoning that giving up feels like losing it. What's the actual risk on an ordered queue?
options: It guarantees every message eventually gets processed successfully
It has no real downside, since the queue naturally smooths out variance over time
It's the correct approach regardless of whether the queue enforces ordering
One bad message that never succeeds blocks every message behind it indefinitely, stalling the whole partition
mcqs.explanation: On an ordered queue or partition, an unbounded retry doesn't just fail to process the bad message — it prevents anything behind it from processing at all. There's no guarantee of eventual success for a genuinely poisoned message, and the correct approach differs specifically because ordering creates this blocking risk that an unordered queue wouldn't have in the same way.
